messages:
ana: EU canary showing big LCP regressions on /customers/map when choropleth is visible. Noticed ~21:05 UTC.
joel: I pulled a flamegraph — main thread spends a ton of time parsing a ~140KB chunk that now includes `topojson-client` + telemetry helper. Paint went 80ms -> 1.1s.
miriam: We recently changed client prefetch strategy to eager in the telemetry rollout; with many map widgets that results in duplicate fetches and chunk-parse thrash across isolates. Prefetch hitrate collapsed to ~16% on canary.
devops-bot: deploy: telemetry-sidecar v2.9.0 -> canary at 2025-07-02T21:10:03Z; status: success
joel: Quick experiments in staging: adding header `x-prefetch-policy: conservative` on the canary route drops paint to ~140ms. No code rollback needed.
ana: (typo) ana: That sounds promising — conservative prefetch reduces duplicate downloads but raises cold latency slightly.
miriam: I can open a tiny routing PR to inject header for the canary and reorder imports to decouple topojson from telemetry helper so chunk sizes shrink.
joel: Also proposed: emit `client.chunk.parse_ms` with labels (chunk_name, canary) so we can pinpoint parse hotspots.
ana: ana: Good call. Add a dashboard tile for per-chunk p50/p95. If the header fix doesn't hold, Plan A is flip canary to previous sidecar revision via routing; Plan B is code rollback.
devops-bot: alert: canary frontend LCP p95 +0.9%; routing alert posted to #incidents
miriam: PR ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7992 — routing override + import reorder + metric. Will deploy to canary and watch.
ana: ana: Deploying PR now, monitoring metrics.
